title: Answer to Question: America Moves Its Fleet to the Asia-Pacific Region
text:
Answer to Question

Question:

On 1/6/2012 the US Defence Secretary Leon Panetta announced at a security conference in Singapore that "the United States will keep six aircraft carriers in the Asia/Pacific region and will move 60% of its warships to the region during the coming years up to 2020. He explained that the moving of the American fleets comes in the context of implementing a new American strategy aimed at raising the level of the American military presence in the Asia/Pacific region". So what is the reason for America moving most of its naval warships to the Asia/Pacific region? Has America come to take great account of China at the present time or in the coming years? And when might China move to impose its control over that region?

Answer:

To answer that, we mention the following:

1- The Asia/Pacific region includes countries of importance:

- Such as Japan, China, Taiwan and the two Koreas, North and South. Among these countries there is a dispute over the question of sovereignty over the East China Sea, a dispute over some of the islands in it, and over freedom of navigation and fishing.

- And such as the Philippines, Vietnam, Cambodia, Thailand, Brunei, Malaysia, Singapore and Indonesia. Among these countries there is a dispute over the question of sovereignty over the South China Sea and a dispute over some of the islands in it, in addition to the Strait of Malacca and freedom of navigation and fishing.

- Moreover, the region is considered an extension of the Indian Ocean, on whose northern coasts lie Burma, Bangladesh and India, until it reaches Pakistan, which is nearer to the Arabian Sea, which is an extension of the Indian Ocean. Then comes the Gulf of Oman, reaching the Gulf region, and to the south as far as the Gulf of Aden and then Bab al-Mandab, reaching the Red Sea, from which one crosses to the Mediterranean Sea.

- In addition, the Asia/Pacific region, together with the northern coasts of the Indian Ocean, has the greatest population density in the world and the greatest population density of Muslims; in this region there is close to half of the world's population and half of the number of Muslims.

2- Sea routes are considered more important than land routes, because a greater quantity can be carried by ships, the cost is lower, and ships sail easily away from the border barriers of states, except for transit through straits or sea passages that are under the control of the states overseeing them. Until today 90% of goods are still transported by sea routes by ships, despite the development of land routes and the manufacture of huge trucks, and likewise the development of air transport, but it is costly and cannot carry quantities as much as ships carry. And 65% of oil is transported across the seas by ships, despite the development in laying pipelines. That is why the Pacific Ocean has great importance, as it extends to the Indian Ocean, through which 70% of the oil and gas supplies from the Gulf region to those countries pass, and the need of this region, especially China and India, for oil will double in the coming decade. And there is the Malacca passage, which is considered an important passage between the two oceans and extends for a distance of 800 km between the Malaysian peninsula and the Indonesian island of Sumatra; about 40% of world goods pass through it, as well as half of the world trade in oil and gas, and it is important for China and India for the transit of goods east and west. So this region is of extreme importance in terms of the presence of the sea routes...

3- Moreover, this region is important from the strategic aspect. China is working to establish its hegemony or control over this region because it considers it its region historically and geographically, apart from its strategic and economic importance for it. China is a major regional state and is working to be influential in this region, but it has not been able to impose its control over it. American control and hegemony are still the greatest and the strongest in influence. America was concerned with this region in the period of the Cold War because of the threat to it from the Soviet Union at that time, since Russia has maritime borders in the north of the Pacific Ocean. In that period America had more than 600 warships, and when the Cold War ended with the fall of Communism, the break-up of the Soviet Union and the disappearance of its danger, America reduced the number of its warships to less than half, the number reaching 279, and in 2008 the number settled at 285 warships. It contented itself with this number since there was no longer a competitor to it or anyone threatening its presence in this region.

This is in addition to America having a fixed military presence in military bases in Japan and South Korea, which lie on the coasts of the East China Sea, and it likewise has the like of that in the Philippines, which lies on the coasts of the South China Sea. It has about a quarter of a million soldiers in the region... and it has had a fixed military presence in the region since the fifties of the last century.

4- In the light of the shaking of America's position globally following the defeats it tasted in Iraq and Afghanistan at the hands of the Muslims, and following the financial crisis that exploded in 2008, China began to assess the situation and to work to exploit it to increase its strength, so that it could impose its influence in its region if America collapsed completely, or suffered a shock stronger than the one that occurred such that it could not preserve its influence in that region, or if the Muslims expelled it from the region.

Although America realises that China is not a major global state, and so does not work to dislodge it from the position of the first state in the world, it is a major regional state, that is, in the Asia/Pacific region, which China considers its region and which is important for it economically and strategically. China works to be the holder of sovereignty in the East China Sea, and if it succeeds in that it would make Japan and South Korea at its mercy or under its hegemony, in addition to North Korea, over which it has influence. China also works to have sovereignty over the South China Sea, so that it makes the Philippines, Vietnam, Cambodia, Laos, Brunei, Malaysia, Singapore and Indonesia under its influence or under its hegemony, and then it would control the Strait of Malacca, which is considered a lifeline for it. And if China controls this region, or imposes its influence, or puts it under its hegemony, then it would be able to influence the Indian Ocean region and seriously threaten American influence in the region. This is a fateful issue for America; it will never allow that to happen, whatever exorbitant costs it may cost it.

5- America gives importance to protecting its territory from the two sides of the Atlantic Ocean and the Pacific Ocean, which surround it. Since there is currently no threat worth mentioning to America in the Atlantic, because the European states are not currently undertaking any serious work in which they compete with America in the Atlantic Ocean or beyond the Atlantic to the west, that is, in South America, and America does not expect in the foreseeable term any actual serious competition from Europe in the Atlantic or beyond it, America therefore currently gives importance to other regions, namely the Pacific Ocean and the Indian Ocean and what follows from it of the Arabian Sea, the Gulf and Bab al-Mandab.. That is why it has reduced its force in the Atlantic in favour of its force in the Pacific Ocean, as Panetta mentioned in the details, that 60% of the naval force will be in the Asia/Pacific region by 2020, and that includes 6 aircraft carriers and most of the American cruisers, destroyers, combat ships and submarines. He referred to the disputes between the states of the region and China, saying: "The position of the United States is clear: we call for restraint and a diplomatic solution; we oppose provocation, coercion and the use of force." And he claimed that "his country does not take sides with one party against another" (the American agency UPI, 2/6/2012). This agency pointed out that "the American President Barack Obama said in November that the Asia/Pacific region is a top priority for the United States". And this agency mentioned that "the American focus on the region comes in the light of the rise of China and India as two global economic powers, and after the American withdrawal from Iraq and the approaching withdrawal of American forces from Afghanistan".

Moreover, America's increase of its naval military presence in the Asia/Pacific region enables it to increase the volume of the exercises and manoeuvres it conducts there in the coming years. America also plans to increase the visits of American naval vessels to wider areas of the Pacific Ocean, so as to include the Indian Ocean. It is mentioned that "the American armed forces took part during the past year in 172 training operations and war manoeuvres (in this region) that included 24 countries" (BBC, 2/6/2012).

6- The American military strategy in the Asia/Pacific region, which the US Defence Secretary announced, came within the new military strategy of America that the American President Obama announced on 6/1/2012, which focused on three main axes: the first, reducing the number of American forces in Europe; the second, reducing defence spending while preserving qualitative superiority; and the third, focusing on the Pacific region in order to avert the growing power of China, while giving importance to the region of the Middle East and Asia. Since there is no danger or threat to America in Europe, there is no need for the presence of large numbers of American soldiers there within the plan of reducing military spending, because America is still groaning under the weight of the financial crisis and has not been able to get out of it. So it adopted a plan of reducing military spending over the next ten years by the amount of 1.2 trillion dollars, and of increasing its forces in the Asia/Pacific region.

Thus the increase of American naval forces in the Asia/Pacific region is directed basically towards China and its expected danger to America's influence in the region.

7- But there is another matter that the movements of the American naval forces suggest, and the spread of its bases in the Pacific Ocean, passing through the Strait of Malacca to the Indian Ocean, then the Arabian Sea, the Gulf and the Red Sea... that is, not restricted to the coasts of China and its seas... This matter is what America takes into its reckoning of the expected emergence of an Islamic power in the region, "the Khilafah State", which makes America take account of the existing power of China and the expected power of the Islamic State... That is why it extends with its bases and its movements along the length of the coasts of the Islamic region... It is laying out the possibilities of the coming changes in the coming years and in the next decade, of the appearance of a great Islamic power in the Islamic world, especially as half of the number of Muslims is in the Asia/Pacific region and in the north of the Indian Ocean, and it is an extension of the regions of the Muslims in the Gulf, in the Middle East and in Africa; indeed it is a great strategic depth for the Islamic State when it is established, by the permission of Allah. It is worth mentioning that the Islamic State began from its first eras to work to reach that region in order to spread good throughout its lands, so it became almost an Islamic region, until the Western colonialists came and began to spread the seeds of evil in it, so that they could colonise it and control it, for three centuries, in order to break the back of the Muslims from the east, at the same time as they were waging colonial wars and conspiracies against the Muslims in the west, so that they could finish off their state, the Khilafah State, and its Islamic system. And all of that was achieved for them... And they fear its return anew... And it is returning, by the permission of Allah, and indeed tomorrow is near for the one who watches for it.
